problem: After global CLI-selected authentication modes are available, the better-auth placeholder needs a working account provider without adding a persistent Next.js server or requiring the provider in the MIT Community package.

risk.rollback: Disable account entry points without opening access, retain provider account data, and use explicit local CLI recovery into token mode. Missing or invalid entitlement must never turn the installation anonymous.

scope: Implement stage 2 of NOTE-20260909-self-hosted-saas-plan/authentication-modes-and-plugin.md after the shared mode/provider boundary: an optional separately distributed Better Auth integration package.

First deliver one owner account with username/password login, whole-product sessions, logout, password change and local CLI recovery. Multi-user roles, organizations, public signup, email delivery, billing and SaaS tenancy are later slices.

Use a versioned MIT provider contract with controller-owned authorization and stable Switcher principal IDs. Explicit local plugin loading validates compatibility and provides lifecycle disposal; do not build a general plugin marketplace.

Mount Better Auth in the existing Node controller and preserve the static dashboard. Select a small core login screen or plugin-owned prebuilt static assets without bundling proprietary server implementation into Community.

Integrate provider storage and migrations with the single controller-owned SQLite connection. Validate adapter transaction and disposal behavior before implementation. PostgreSQL is not a prerequisite.
Resolve account provisioning before committing the username-only UX: the standard Better Auth username signup still requires email. Keep public registration disabled and provide local CLI recovery.

Verify password/session lifecycle, login rate limiting, safe cookies, origin/CSRF, HTTPS for remote password entry and invalidation across API, knowledge, downloads and SSE. Machine clients keep non-password credentials.

Separate plugin distribution from license entitlement. The core remains MIT and Better Auth retains its MIT notices. A proprietary integration and a later offline license file are candidates, not an approved commercial license or activation-server requirement.
Missing, incompatible or failed providers never fall back to anonymous access. Explicit CLI recovery to token mode preserves user data; Community remains installable and usable without the plugin.
title: Add optional Better Auth plugin for username and password login
trigger: Begin after stage 1 global modes and provider contract pass acceptance; use the first owner login workflow to prove the plugin boundary.
validation: Install the plugin against the supported core API, provision the owner, log in once and exercise runtime plus knowledge without a second credential.
Verify logout, password change/reset and account/session revocation invalidate access through all browser/API/SSE/download paths; CLI recovery works without email or a hosted activation service.
Verify login limits, uniform authentication failures, cookie/origin protections and remote HTTPS behavior using the actual pinned library configuration.
Verify shared SQLite ownership, migration ordering, upgrade/backup/restore and plugin disposal without an extra database connection or controller.
Verify absent/incompatible/crashing plugins fail closed and explicit return to token mode preserves data.

Build/install the Community artifact without private implementation and the plugin-enabled artifact with required dependency notices. Run relevant tests, pnpm check, build, browser and clean package verification.
value: One reusable account integration supports paid self-hosted packaging and later hosted onboarding while keeping the MIT local product independent.
